\section{Documentation survey of IED security capabilities}\label{app:crawler}

\paragraph{Collection.} A crawler listed every protective relay, controller or RTU, PLC and power meter in the public online catalogues of SEL, Schneider Electric, Rockwell Automation, GE Vernova and Siemens as of 13 October 2026 (484 devices) and recorded each device\textquotesingle s lifecycle state from the vendor\textquotesingle s own wording on its product page. A stratified random sample of up to four devices per vendor, device category and lifecycle state (fixed seed; 99 devices) was then crawled: product pages and the public data sheets, manuals and device profiles they link to, within a fixed page budget per device. The crawler reads only documents that are public, honours robots.txt, and stores the SHA-256 hash and retrieval time of every document, so each quotation below can be checked against the exact bytes read.

\paragraph{Review.} For each device and capability (authentication, integrity, encryption, DNP3 Secure Authentication, TLS, IPsec, CIP Security, SSH), a reviewer recorded one of four results---supported, conditional, explicitly unsupported or unknown---for each interface, keeping control protocols (e.g., DNP3, IEC~61850, IEC~60870-5-104, Modbus, EtherNet/IP) apart from management access (web, engineering tools, user login). Every supported or conditional result cites a verbatim passage, checked mechanically against the retained text. An unknown is never read as absence of the capability. The results were drafted with an AI assistant and checked a second time against every retained passage; the authors\textquotesingle{} confirmation is pending.
% UPDATE the sentence above once the authors have confirmed the devices in Table~\ref{tab:crawler-devices}.

\paragraph{Limits.} The counts describe what the retrieved public documents say about catalogue entries. They are not market shares, they say nothing about installed devices or enabled settings, and they are lower bounds: the crawler reads a few documents per device, and a vendor may document more elsewhere. For example, the sampled crawl retrieved two flyers for the SEL Real-Time Automation Controller (RTAC), while an SEL application guide retrieved in our pilot documents DNP3 over TLS for it. Two of the six devices with documented encryption, the SICAM A8000 series and its CP-8050 unit, are separate catalogue entries that rest on the same catalogue page.

\paragraph{DNP3.} Table~\ref{tab:crawler-dnp3} restricts the sample to the 32 devices whose own retrieved documents name DNP3, and Table~\ref{tab:crawler-dnp3-devices} lists them. ``Plaintext'' means that no DNP3 security is documented: DNP3 then travels readable unless something outside the device protects it. DNP3 Secure Authentication authenticates messages and does not encrypt them. The plaintext count is an upper bound, because a document the crawl did not retrieve may name DNP3 security; the SEL RTAC is one such case. The percentages are shares of the sampled devices, not of installed devices or of traffic.
